records.region: Wollaston Peninsula, southwestern Victoria Island; regional Kugaluk River–Penny Bay setting.
records.material_pending_reason: No actually inspected permitted detailed source establishes the chosen opening, intervening lakes/channels and joins, and the actual selected coastward endpoint.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Source-supported regional Kugaluk River crossing Wollaston Peninsula to Penny Bay. The candidate is not yet established for the complete selected eastern opening, inland succession or actual terminal.
records.completion_scope: All34 selected parts were considered in bounded source research. Only the named regional Kugaluk–Penny Bay setting is supported; no component is marked geographically complete from a regional location figure or unseen image.
records.supported_name_scope: NASA article prose names the river and receiving bay; Memoir434 Figure1B independently labels them in the regional setting. No name is imposed on every selected lake, feeder or channel.

scope_limits: Kugaluk is a source-supported regional candidate, not a completed representative-system result or a formally verified registry name.
The chosen opening, lake passages, side-stream joins and actual selected endpoint lack ordinary-scale primary source correspondence; individual names remain unestablished.
Penny Bay is named as Kugaluk River’s receiver in actually read prose, but that fact alone does not match the selected final channel.
No present discharge, tidal state, perennial flow, seasonal passability, exact bank, modern shoreline or official hydronym boundary is established.
The same-named mainland Kugaluk River associated with Liverpool Bay is a different geographic setting and is not used to identify this selection.

records.candidate_name_role: no_primary_river_name_established; Bluenose Lake is a bounded lake-component identity
records.material_pending_reason: The very first southwestern selected opening before the eastward feeder and Bluenose Lake inlet is not unambiguously established by the inspected thematic map. The lake, northern outlet and remaining river-to-Amundsen-Gulf corridor are supported at ordinary scale.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No representative river name established from actually read primary material. Bluenose Lake is supported for the traversed lake component only.
records.completion_scope: Original NTGS thematic cartography establishes the Bluenose Lake passage, its northward outlet river, the middle/lower corridor and the Amundsen Gulf terminal. The selected initial southwestern opening remains unestablished. No primary river hydronym is accepted; the lake label does not name the whole system.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative river name established from actually read primary material. Bluenose Lake is supported for the traversed lake component only.

scope_limits: The chosen southwestern initial opening is not continuously established by the available thematic figure; this single material gap prevents a completed geographic review or completed naming-scope hold.
Croker River is a discovery-only lead for the northward Bluenose outlet. It was not directly named in the actually read primary map and is not an accepted candidate or registry finding.
The original figure is a regional thaw-slump study map rather than a detailed hydrographic survey. River reaches are unlabeled; a lake label cannot be extended to the whole selected system.
No lake-management or artificial-connector identity was established; modern operations, present flow conditions and exact bank or mouth positions are outside this bounded result.
Previous pre-reset source maps are not asserted to survive. Earlier findings for other targets were not treated as new route proof.

records.region: Northeastern Greenland, Inland Ice and Hagen Bræ to the J. C. Christensen Land–Academy Land terrain and Independence Fjord.
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river identity established. Hagen Bræ is glacier context, Academy Land is land-region context, and Independence Fjord is the receiving-water context only.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The national original supplies the southern opening omitted by the regional sheet, with overlapping source coverage. The regional original covers the entire continuation through glacier, exposed-rock, interior-ice and Quaternary-covered terrain to the actual Independence Fjord endpoint. This complete geographic correspondence does not establish a representative named natural river.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected object starts south of the Peary Land regional map, runs north through the inland-ice and Hagen Bræ setting, turns west and northwest through mapped ice, exposed rock and Quaternary-covered passages, then crosses the Academy Land coastal belt and ends in Independence Fjord. The neighboring Academy Gletscher and Astrup Fjord are distinct context features, not whole-system river names.
records.completion_scope: All 53 stored parts, every join, the chosen opening, the regional map-edge crossing, all mapped terrain transitions and the actual selected endpoint were read against the available originals. No material geographic interval remains unviewed at ordinary source scale. Source epochs and thematic limits prevent exact contemporary hydraulic, ice-front, bank or mouth claims.

component_scope_limits: Named glacier, land-region and fjord features have distinct feature types; no such label is assigned as the river-group name.
Quaternary cover, pale ice units, geological contacts and national ice/sub-ice contours do not establish natural-river through-links.
The actual modeled endpoint is geographically within Independence Fjord, but a natural river mouth along this selected line is not established.
The map spelling Academy Land is retained as source context, without claiming current formal registry verification.
A null candidate means that this research did not establish a name; it does not assert that no local or official name exists.

records.material_pending_reason: The southern transfer from the western headward lake-and-stream loop into Kinguk Lake remains unresolved. The subsequent lake chain and Kommanik downstream component are supported; the actual selected endpoint lies before the mapped continuation toward Gibson Bay.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Named downstream reach on the Cory Bay sheet; not yet a completed representative identity for the entire selected lake-and-stream system.
records.completion_scope: Primary historical land-use cartography supports Kommanik River for the downstream selected component and identifies the middle and lower lake chain. A material southern transfer from the western headward lake loop into Kinguk Lake remains unresolved, so the whole selected system remains source-material pending.
records.supported_name_scope: Named downstream reach on the Cory Bay sheet; not yet a completed representative identity for the entire selected lake-and-stream system.

scope_limits: The unresolved southern through-connection prevents completed representative-system identity and completed naming-scope hold.
Kommanik River is directly visible on the lower map component; the candidate is not extended as a scalar name to the unnamed headward reaches or the several separately named lakes.
The source spelling Kavivau Lake is preserved without asserting a modern standardized or formal registry spelling.

The two historical sheets use 1980 topographic bases and 1986 thematic cartography; the introduction states that the South Baffin resource information was current to December1984 and that some information was interim or reconnaissance-based.
The finding does not establish current channel conditions, flow direction or rates, exact banks, exact lake naming boundaries, or formal name registration.
A discovery snippet, catalogued name, nearby label, source viewport coverage or pinned modeled line is not independent proof of the unresolved selected transfer.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
